hints: Focus on how atomic radius changes across Period 3, from Na on the left to Cl on the right.
Element Y must be chlorine, since atomic radius decreases across the period to a minimum at Cl.
Think about melting points in Period 3, Si is giant covalent and very high while P, S, Cl and Ar are simple molecular and very low, so which element has exactly two elements melting lower than it?
walkthrough:
**Identify element Y from atomic radius**

Think across Period 3 from left to right. More protons pull the same shell in tighter, so radius gets smaller.

Trend: $\text{Na} > \text{Mg} > \text{Al} > \text{Si} > \text{P} > \text{S} > \text{Cl}$

So the smallest atomic radius is chlorine. That gives $Y = \text{Cl}$.

**Identify element Z from melting point**

Now think about structure and melting point. Si has the highest melting point (giant covalent), Mg and Al are high (metallic), while P, S, Cl and Ar are low (simple molecular).

Actual order from low to high is roughly: $\text{Ar} < \text{Cl} < \text{P} < \text{Na} < \text{S} < \text{Mg} < \text{Al} < \text{Si}$

Only two elements melt lower than Z, so Z must be the third lowest. That is phosphorus. So $Z = \text{P}$.

**Combine Y and Z to find R**

We have $Y = \text{Cl}$ and $Z = \text{P}$ reacting together.

Phosphorus and chlorine form covalent chlorides:
$$\text{P} + \text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{PCl}_3$$

So compound R must be a phosphorus chloride.

options.A: MgCl2 needs Mg and Cl. Mg is neither Y (Cl) nor Z (P), so this cannot be formed from Y and Z alone.
options.B: MgS needs Mg and S. Neither matches Y = Cl or Z = P. Students who mix up high melting point metals with low melting point non-metals may pick this.
options.C: Na2S needs Na and S. Na has the largest (not smallest) radius in Period 3, and S does not fit the melting point clue for Z.
options.D: PCl3 is formed from P and Cl. This fits perfectly with Y = Cl (smallest radius) and Z = P (third lowest melting point, only Ar and Cl are lower).
